meta.title: The Journey
meta.description: How KUL Enterprises started. Jamaica, the Air Force, eleven years driving for other carriers, and the first truck of his own. The story behind the carrier in {location}.

pinnedStatement: None of this is a sales argument. It is here because a carrier is a person, and the person hauling your freight spent eleven years learning the job on somebody else's trucks before he bought his own.

chapterOne.heading: Jamaica
paragraphs: My mother brought my sister and me to America. She told us we were spending the summer with our father.
chapterOne.imageAlt: Mark Brown and his sister in Jamaica, early 1980s

chapterFive.heading: Eleven years, other people's trucks
chapterFive.body: Every photograph from here on is one he took through a windscreen. They run in the order the light does, because that is the order he saw them in.

frames.alt: An interstate at night, headlights and lane markings drawing forward
frames.line: I thought I was learning how to drive a truck.

frames.alt: Mountain peaks in violet light before sunrise
frames.line: What I didn't realize was that the road was teaching me something far greater.

frames.alt: A grey blue sky lifting over the interstate before sunrise
frames.line: Every mile introduced me to a new place.

frames.alt: A road running into low mist at dawn
frames.line: Every state introduced me to different people.

frames.alt: A band of sunrise colour along the horizon above the highway
frames.line: Every delivery reminded me that trust travels farther than freight.

frames.alt: The sun breaking the horizon at the end of a straight road
frames.line: I had a plan. But plans have a way of changing.

frames.alt: A desert highway bending out of sight
frames.line: There were victories. There were setbacks. Both became teachers.

frames.alt: Traffic across several lanes of interstate in daylight
frames.line: I wasn't chasing titles. I was learning to become dependable.

frames.alt: A wide horizon opening out on both sides of the road
frames.line: Freight moved every day. But what truly kept the industry moving wasn't trucks. It was people.

frames.alt: A highway curving through a rock cut under a bright sky
frames.line: Every load represented someone's trust. Every mile represented someone's promise.

frames.alt: The road running on with the sun high and no destination visible
frames.line: The farther I traveled, the more I realized every person has a story.

contactSheet.statement: He did not photograph the road once. He photographed it for eleven years, and these are the ones that survived the cut.

chapterSix.heading: One truck of his own
paragraphs: Every company begins with paperwork. But that's not where KUL began. KUL began with a promise.
We didn't build this company to be the biggest. We built it to be trusted.
chapterSix.footnote: KUL Enterprises LLC, from 2026. One tractor, one driver, and a phone number that reaches the person driving it.
chapterSix.imageWideAlt: A two lane road running on through dense pine forest
chapterSix.imageInsetAlt: A road seen from height, running down through a valley
chapterSix.imageInsetCaption: There is no photograph of the KUL tractor here yet.

close.heading: About the photographs
paragraphs: Every image on this page is one Mark took himself, and none of it has been staged, bought or generated. Three of the six chapters have no photograph of what they describe, because none was ever taken: the construction sites, leaving home and the Air Force carry pictures from his own archive instead, and the words carry the rest.
The words are his too. They come from the story he wrote out for this page, kept as he wrote it.
